chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever enters [the state of] ihram for Umrah alone [without combining it with Hajj] should cease the Talbiyah when the camels place their hooves in the Haram [sanctuary]."

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: The ritual proclamation of 'Labbayk' (Here I am, O God) recited during Hajj and Umrah.
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The sacred sanctuary area of Mecca.
key_terms.مُفْرِدًا: A pilgrim who performs Umrah independently, separate from Hajj.

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim performing Umrah alone stop reciting the Talbiyah?
ai.summary: In the Shia scholarly tradition, this narration from Al-Tahdhib clarifies the precise temporal boundary for the Mufrid, distinguishing it from the Qarun who combines Hajj and Umrah. The cessation of Talbiyah upon the mount's hooves touching the ground in the Haram signifies the formal entry into the sacred state, a detail emphasized by jurists to ensure ritual correctness during the transition from the Miqat to the sanctuary.
